# OAuthGuide

**Live OAuth setup guides for any app — generated by an AI agent.**

A developer submits any app name. An agent searches official documentation and community discussions, extracts structured information, and returns a complete guide covering setup steps, approval requirements, time estimates, known blockers, and what it verified.

---

## Setup

### 1. Clone & install

```bash
git clone <repo-url>
cd oauth-guide
bun install
```

### 2. Configure environment

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

Edit `.env.local` with your keys:

```bash
EXA_API_KEY=        # https://exa.ai — semantic web search
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=  # https://firecrawl.dev — doc crawling
GEMINI_API_KEY=     # https://aistudio.google.com — AI extraction
```

### 3. Run

```bash
bun dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)

---

## How it works

```
Input: App name
  → Exa finds the official OAuth docs URL
  → Firecrawl reads the full docs page
  → Exa searches community discussions (Reddit, GitHub, blogs)
  → Gemini extracts structured guide from all sources
  → Guide renders with difficulty score, steps, blockers, sources
```

---

## Key decisions

**All dynamic, no static guides.** Every guide is generated live from real docs at request time. This means guides are always current — no staleness from a pre-built library.

**Two sources, clearly labeled.** Official documentation is always separated from community reports. Developers can see exactly where each piece of information comes from.

**Schema-driven extraction.** Gemini fills a strict JSON schema rather than writing free-form text. This keeps every guide consistent and comparable across apps.

**Difficulty scoring is computed, not guessed.** The score (1–5) is derived from what the agent finds: prerequisites, review process, verification requirements, and audit requirements.

---

## Limitations

- Guide quality depends on how well the provider documents their OAuth flow
- Community signal coverage varies by app popularity
- Approval wait times are estimates — official docs and community reports may differ
- Some providers require login to access developer portals, which the agent cannot navigate

---

## Stack

- **Next.js 14** — framework
- **Exa** — semantic web search
- **Firecrawl** — documentation crawling
- **Gemini 2.0 Flash** — structured extraction
- **Tailwind CSS** — styling
- **Vercel** — hosting
